notes.summary: Distance = Speed × Time. Trains, boats and average speed are all built on this one idea. 1–2 questions per tier.

concepts.title: Units
concepts.body: km/h to m/s: multiply by 5/18. m/s to km/h: multiply by 18/5.

concepts.title: Trains
concepts.body: Crossing a pole or man: distance = train length. Crossing a platform or another train: distance = sum of lengths. Relative speed: add for opposite directions, subtract for the same direction.

concepts.title: Boats and streams
concepts.body: Downstream = u + v, Upstream = u − v. So boat speed u = (D + U)/2, stream speed v = (D − U)/2.

varieties.name: Speed, unit change and average speed
varieties.how: Average speed = total distance / total time. Equal distances: 2xy/(x + y).

varieties.name: Trains
varieties.how: Time = (sum of lengths) / relative speed, in m and m/s.

example.q: A 200 m train at 72 km/h crosses a pole in?
Downstream 10 km/h, upstream 6 km/h. Boat speed in still water?

tips: Always convert to the same units before dividing.
For equal distances at speeds x and y, average speed = 2xy/(x + y).
traps: Average speed is NOT (x + y)/2 when the distances are equal.
For a platform, add the platform length to the train length.

questions.q: A speed of 72 km/h is equal to:
A car covers 360 km in 4 hours 30 minutes. What is its speed?
A train 150 m long is running at 54 km/h. How long will it take to cross a platform 300 m long?
A boat goes downstream at 18 km/h and upstream at 12 km/h. What is the speed of the stream?
Two trains 120 m and 180 m long are running in opposite directions at 40 km/h and 50 km/h. In how many seconds will they cross each other?
questions.solution:
Relative speed = 40 + 50 = 90 km/h = 90 × 5/18 = 25 m/s.
Distance = 120 + 180 = 300 m.
Time = 300/25 = 12 s.

questions.q: A man goes from A to B at 40 km/h and returns from B to A at 60 km/h. What is his average speed for the whole journey?
questions.solution:
Equal distances, so average speed = 2xy/(x + y).
= 2 × 40 × 60 / 100 = 48 km/h.
